30251.text: Which among the following halide/s will not show S N 1 reaction:
30251.sol: Vinylic halides are organic compounds containing their halogen atom bonded to one of the two carbon atoms in the double bond present in that molecule. 47247.subject: Biology
47247.text: Given below are two statements. Statement I: There is less species biodiversity in tropical latitudes than in temperate region. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true, but Statement II is false
Statement I is false, but Statement II is true
47247.sol: Statement I is false because tropical latitudes have greater species biodiversity compared to temperate regions. The favorable environmental conditions in the tropics support a higher number of species. Statement II is true because tropical environments are less seasonal, relatively more constant, and predictable compared to temperate regions. This constant environment promotes niche specialization and leads to greater species diversity. Therefore, Statement I is false, but Statement II is true. Answer: Statement I

65585.text: The value of alternating e.m.f. (E) in the given circuit is

The resistor voltage is in phase with the current, while the inductor voltage leads by 90^ and the capacitor voltage lags by 90^ . Thus V_L and V_C differ in phase by 180^ . 79654.subject: Botany
79654.sol: Viroids are small, circular, single stranded RNA molecules that are the smallest known pathogens. The extracellular form of the viroid is naked RNA, ie, there is no protein capsid of any kind. No viroid diseases of animals are known and the precise mechanisms by which viroids cause plant diseases remain unclear.

84097.sol: In ECG, P-wave indicates impulse of contraction generated by SA-node and it spreads in atria causing atrial depolarisation. Activating cyclic AMP located on the cell membrane.
Using aquaporin channels as second messenger.
84218.sol: Hormones are chemicals which are produced and secreted by endocrine glands in the body. Hormones are given out into the bloodstream which travel to other parts of the body where they bring about specific responses from certain cells. The steroid hormones are obtained from cholesterol and are lipid-soluble in nature. Sex hormones (androgens, estrogens, and progesterone) produced by male and female gonads and hormones of the adrenal glands (aldosterone, cortisol, and androgens) are examples of steroid hormones. 84260.text: Which of the following statement is correct in relation to the endocrine system?

Organs in the body like gastrointestinal tract, heart, kidney and liver do not produce any hormones
Non-nutrient chemicals produced by the body in trace amount that act as intercellular messenger are known as h
Releasing and inhibitory hormones are produced by the pituitary gland
84260.sol: Hormones are non nutrient chemicals, which act as intracellular messengers and are produced in trace amounts. Endocrine cells are present in different parts of the gastrointestinal tract, e.g., gastrin, secretin, GIP. Atrial wall of our heart secretes a peptide hormone called ANF (Atrial Natriuretic Factor), RH / HH are produced by hypothalamus. Adenohypophysis is not directly under neural control, it is under the control of hypothalamic hormones, brought by portal system.

84465.subject: Zoology
84465.text: Which of the following statements is correct about Plasmodium ?
options: Fertilization takes place in mosquito gut
84465.sol: In the life cycle of Plasmodium , asexual reproduction takes place in the human host (in liver cells and red blood cells). The sexual stages, known as gametocytes, develop in the red blood cells of the human host. When a female Anopheles mosquito bites an infected person, it takes up these gametocytes along with the blood meal. Fertilization and further development of the gametes take place in the gut (stomach) of the mosquito.

84576.subject: Zoology

84576.sol: At ovulation, the mammalian ovum (in the secondary oocyte stage) is released from the Graafian follicle. It is surrounded by two main coverings: 1. Zona pellucida: An inner, non-cellular glycoprotein layer secreted by the oocyte. 2. Corona radiata: An outer, cellular layer formed by the follicular cells (granulosa cells).

84851.subject: Zoology
84851.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In eukaryotes there are three RNA polymerases in the nucleus in addition to the RNA polymerase found in the organelles. options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
84851.sol: In eukaryotes, there are at least three RNA polymerase in the nucleus (in addition to the RNA polymerase found in the organelles). There is clear cut division of labour. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, and 5.8 S ), whereas the RNA polymerase III is responsible for transcription of tRNA, 5 SrRNA and SnRNAs. The RNA polymerase II transcribes precursor of mRNA. Hence statement I and statement II, both are correct.

Used for broadcasting radio and television programs
104264.sol: The electromagnetic wave produced by the sudden deceleration of high-speed electrons when they strike a heavy metal target is the X-ray. options: I and III, but not II
I and II, but not III
II and III, but not I
125738.sol: C ₄ -plants have an alternative CO ₂ fixation pathway called Hatch and Slack cycle. These plants have Kranz anatomy in leaf, where vascular bundles are surrounded by bundle sheath. In C ₄ cycle light reaction occurs in, mesophyll chloroplast by PEP carboxylaes and the assimilation of CO ₂ takes place in, i.e., dark phase in bundle sheath chloroplast by Rubisco.

125953.subject: Botany
125953.text: Where does the embryo develop in the embryo sac?
options: At the base of the embryo sac
At the micropylar end of the embryo sac
At the chalazal end of the embryo sac
In the middle of the embryo sac
125953.sol: Embryo develops at the micropylar end of the embryo sac where the zygote is situated . Most zygotes divide only after certain amount of endosperm is formed. This is an adaptation to provide assured nutrition to the developing embryo. Though the seeds differ greatly, the early stages of embryo development (embryogeny) are similar in both monocotyledons and dicotyledons depicts the stages of embryogeny in a dicotyledonous embryo. The zygote gives rise to the proembryo and subsequently to the globular, heart-shaped an

options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion

126498.subject: Botany
126498.text: What is the energy required for the substrate to reach the transition state?
126498.sol: One need not supply energy (by heating) in order to form the product. However, whether it is an exothermic or spontaneous reaction or an endothermic or energy requiring reaction, the ‘S’ has to go through a much higher energy state or transition state. The difference in average energy content of ‘S’ from that of this transition state is called ‘activation energy’ .

126880.subject: Botany
126880.text: In which one of the following enzymes, is copper necessarily associated as an activator?
126880.sol: The structure of tyrosinase can be divided into three domains: the central domain, the N-terminal domain, and the C -terminal domain. The central domain, which is composed of six conserved histidine residues, contains the CuA and CuB oxidizing ions. Related Theory Tyrosinase is involved in the biosynthesis of melanin in the melanosomes causing pigmentation of skin, hair and eyes in mammals providing the protection against UV. It converts a protein building block (amino acid) called tyrosine to another compound call

127064.subject: Botany
127064.text: Assertion : Pollution is always caused by human activities. Reason : Pollution is not different from contamination.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
127064.sol: Pollution may be defined as an undesirable change in the physical, chemical or biological characteristics of air, water and land that may or will harmfully affect human lives or other organism. Pollution can be natural or man made. Natural pollution comes from volcanic eruptions, emission of natural gas, soil erosion, ultraviolet rays, etc. Most of the pollution is man-made. Contamination occurs due to the presence of harmful organisms or their products or undersirable products in a desirable product causing diseas

127170.text: What does the equation log S = log C + Z log A represent?
options: The species richness for a given taxonomic group in a region
The relationship between species richness and area for different taxa
The slope of the regression line for species richness and area
The y:intercept of the regression line for species richness and area
127170.sol: : During his pioneering and extensive explorations in the wilderness of South American jungles, the great German naturalist and geographer Alexander von Humboldt observed that within a region species richness increased with increasing explored area, but only up to a limit. In fact , the relation between species richness and area for a wide variety of taxa (angiosperm plants, birds, bats, freshwater fishes) turns out to be a rectangular hyperbola (Figure13.2). mammals are the lowest in number
birds is the lowest in number
amphibians are more in number compared to birds
127255.sol: mammals are the lowest species among vertebrates Fishes being the maximum in number followed by the birds further followed by the reptiles after which amphibians and mammals being the lowest in number

127328.subject: Botany
127328.text: Read the following statements and choose the following option: 1. Biodiversity hotspots are regions with low species richness and low endemism 2. Initially, 25 biodiversity hotspots were identified globally. 3. Biodiversity hotspots together cover more than 10% of the Earth's land area. 4. India has five biodiversity hotspots.
127328.sol: biodiversity hotspots are regions with high species richness and high endemism. It also states that initially, 25 biodiversity hotspots were identified, and later nine more were added, making a total of 34. The paragraph emphasizes that these hotspots cover less than 2% of the Earth's land area, and India has three major biodiversity hotspots.

127641.subject: Botany
127641.text: What does the following diagram represent?
127641.sol: This is a diagrammatic representation of trophic levels in an ecosystem. Organisms occupy a place in the natural surroundings or in a community according to their feeding relationship with other organisms. Based on the source of their nutrition or food, organisms occupy a specific place in the food chain that is known as their trophic level.

128015.subject: Zoology
128015.text: Which of the following is not true about male reproductive system
options: Consist of a pair of bean shaped yellow testes adhered to upper part of kidney by mesorchium
Vasa efferentia opens into Bidder's canal which communicates with urinogenital tract and opens into cloaca
128015.sol: Frogs have well organised male and female reproductive systems. Male reproductive organs consist of a pair of yellowish ovoid testes, which are found adhered to the upper part of kidneys by a double fold of peritoneum called mesorchium. Vasa efferentia are 10-12 in number that arise from testes.

128017.subject: Zoology
128017.text: Identify the incorrect one in the set of statements
options: Male frogs have a copulatory pad on the first digit of the fore limbs.
In male frogs the ureters and ejaculatory ducts open separately in the cloaca
128017.sol: The frog excretes urea and thus is a ureotelic animal. The hind limbs end in five digits and they are larger and muscular than forelimbs that end in four digits. Feet have webbed digits that help in swimming. Frogs exhibit sexual dimorphism. Male frogs can be distinguished by the presence of sound producing vocal sacs and also a copulatory pad on the first digit of the fore limbs which are absent in female frogs. Two ureters emerge from the kidneys in the male frogs. The ureters act as urinogenital ducts which open

128212.subject: Zoology
128212.text: Assertion : Blood in cockroach is colourless haemolymph with no respiratory pigment. Reason : Respiration in cockroach occurs through diffusion in haemolymph.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
128212.sol: The colourless blood or haemolymph of cockroach has a clear plasma and numerous white corpuscles called haemocytes. Being devoid of any respiratory pigment, it does not serve for gaseous exchange. Its plasma contains about 70 % water. Rest of it is composed of amino acids, uric acid, proteins, sugars, fats, and salts of sodium, potassium, calcium and magnesium. Transportation of these materials between different parts of body is the main function of haemolymph. In all terrestrial insects, like cockroach, every tiss

128732.subject: Zoology
128732.text: Vitamin- B ₁₂ is absorbed primarily in the
128732.sol: The parietal cells of gastric mucosa secrete certain intrinsic factors. This help in the absorption of vitamin- B ₁₂ . It is propelled along the small intestine to the terminal ileum and is absorbed by an active transport process.

128785.subject: Zoology
128785.text: Are red blood cells present in the nucleus in most mammals?
128785.sol: Erythrocytes or red blood cells (RBC) are the most abundant of all the cells in blood. A healthy adult man has, on an average, 5 million to 5.5 million of RBCs mm–3 of blood. RBCs are formed in the red bone marrow in the adults . RBCs are devoid of nucleus in most of the mammals and are biconcave in shape. They have a red colored, iron containing complex protein called haemoglobin, hence the color and name of these cells. A healthy individual has 12-16 gms of haemoglobin in every 100 ml of blood. These molecules pl

128888.subject: Zoology
128888.text: What repeats the events described in the cardiac cycle?
options: The contraction of the ventricles and atria
The relaxation of the ventricles and atria
128888.sol: The ventricles and atria are now again in a relaxed (joint diastole) state, as earlier. Soon the SAN generates a new action potential and the events described above are repeated in that sequence and the process continues.

128901.subject: Zoology
128901.text: How does the body alter the cardiac output?
options: By changing both heart rate and stroke volume
128901.sol: This sequential event in the heart which is cyclically repeated is called the cardiac cycle and it consists of systole and diastole of both the atria and ventricles. As mentioned earlier, the heart beats 72 times per minute, i.e., that many cardiac cycles are performed per minute. From this it could be deduced that the duration of a cardiac cycle is 0.8 seconds. During a cardiac cycle, each ventricle pumps out approximately 70 mL of blood which is called the stroke volume . The stroke volume multiplied by the heart

129073.subject: Zoology
129073.text: A newborn baby suffers from severe anaemia and jaundice due to a condition known as erythroblastosis foetalis. For this condition to occur, what must be the Rh blood group status of the baby's parents?
options: Mother is Rh ⁺ and Father is Rh ⁻
Mother is Rh ⁻ and Father is Rh ⁺
Both Mother and Father are Rh ⁻
Both Mother and Father are Rh ⁺
129073.sol: Erythroblastosis foetalis is caused by Rh incompatibility between an Rh ⁻ mother and an Rh ⁺ foetus. The foetus inherits the Rh ⁺ trait from the father. Therefore, the mother must be Rh ⁻ and the father must be Rh ⁺ . If the mother were Rh ⁺ , she would not produce anti-Rh antibodies upon exposure to the foetal blood, and the condition would not occur. If both were Rh ⁻ , the foetus could not be Rh ⁺ . Answer: Mother is Rh ⁻ and Father is Rh ⁺

129892.text: What is the main function of carbonic anhydrase?

This binding is related to the partial pressure of CO2. pO2 is a major factor which could affect this binding. 130425.subject: Zoology
130425.sol: There are 12 pairs of ribs. Each rib is a thin flat bone connected dorsally to the vertebral column and ventrally to sternum.

130436.subject: Zoology
130436.text: Muscles with characteristic striations and involuntary are
options: muscles in the wall of alimentary canal
130436.sol: Cardiac muscles are found in the walls of the heart and in the walls of large veins. Their fibres show the characters of both unstriped and striped muscle fibres and are involuntary.

130669.subject: Zoology
130669.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion

Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
130669.sol: An alarming growth rate could lead to an absolute scarcity of even the basic requirements, i.e., food, shelter and clothing, in spite of significant progress made in those areas. Therefore, the government was forced to take up serious measures to check this population growth rate.

130982.subject: Zoology
130982.text: Select the correct option regarding the given diagram. Assertion(A): Primary spermatocytes undergo meiosis I to form secondary spermatocytes. Reason (R): Secondary spermatocytes undergo mitosis to form spermatids.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
130982.sol: A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division (reduction division) leading to formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes, which have only 23 chromosomes each. The secondary spermatocytes undergo the second meiotic division to produce four equal, haploid spermatids.

131276.subject: Zoology

The first polar body is extruded when the primary oocyte completes its first meiotic division within the tertiary follicle, just prior to ovulation (A-II). The second polar body is extruded when the secondary oocyte completes its second meiotic division, which is induced by the entry of a sperm (B-III). 131894.subject: Zoology
131894.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The total length of DNA in a typical mammalian cell is approximately 2.2 meters. Reason (R): The mammalian genome contains 6.6 10^9 base pairs and the pitch of the B-DNA helix is 0.34 nm. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
131894.sol: Assertion (A) is true. The total length of DNA in a typical mammalian cell is calculated by multiplying the total number of base pairs ( 6.6 10^9 bp) by the distance between two consecutive base pairs ( 0.34 10⁻⁹ m), which gives approximately 2.2 meters. Reason (R) is false. While it is true that the diploid mammalian genome contains 6.6 10^9 base pairs, the pitch of the B-DNA helix is 3.4 nm, not 0.34 nm. The value 0.34 nm represents the distance between two consecutive base pairs, not the pitch. Answer: Assertion

132276.text: What accumulates in the brain due to the deficiency of the enzyme in the described disorder?

As a result of this phenylalanine is accumulated and converted into phenylpyruvic acid and other derivatives. Accumulation of these in brain results in mental retardation. These are also excreted through urine because of its poor absorption by kidney

132333.subject: Zoology
132333.text: Select the correct statement for the given pedigree.

The pattern of inheritance of Mendelian disorders can be traced in a family by pedigree analysis.
In human genetics, pedigree study is a weak tool, which is utilised to trace the inheritance of a specific tra
By pedigree analysis one can easily understand whether the trait in question is dominant or recessive.

Since it is evident that control crosses that can be performed in pea plants or some other organisms, are not possible in case of human beings, study of the family history about inheritance of a particular trait provides an alternative. Such an analysis of traits in several generations of a family is called the pedigree analysis. In the pedigree analysis the inheritance of a particular trait is repr

132871.subject: Zoology
132871.text: (p+q)2 = p2 + 2pq + q2 = 1 represents an equation used in:
132871.sol: (p+q)2 = p2 + 2pq + q2 = 1 represents an equation used in population genetics proposed by Hardy Weinberg.

133018.subject: Zoology
133018.text: The eyes of Octopus and eyes of cat show different patterns of structure, yet they perform similar function. This is an example of
options: homologous organs that have evolved due to convergent evolution
homologous organs that have evolved due to divergent evolution
analogous organs that have evolved due to convergent evolution
analogous organs that have evolved due to divergent evolution
133018.sol: The analogous organs are not anatomically similar structures through they perform similar functions. Hence, analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution different structures evolving for the same function and hence, having similarity. Homologous organs developed along different direction due to adaptations to different needs. This is divergent evolution and the structures are homologous.

133296.subject: Zoology
133296.text: What is the importance of identifying genes in individuals with inherited susceptibility to certain cancers?
options: To detect genes in individuals with inherited susceptibility to certain cancers
To examine a tissue under a microscope
133296.sol: Biopsy is a procedure where a piece of the suspected tissue is cut into thin sections and is stained and examined under a microscope (histopathological studies) by a pathologist.Early detection of cancers is essential as it allows the disease to be treated successfully in many cases.Antibodies against cancer-specific antigens are used for the detection of certain cancers. Identification of genes in individuals with inherited susceptibility to certain cancers may be very helpful in the prevention of cancers. Such in

133418.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option 1. Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae are responsible for pneumonia in humans. 2. Typhoid Mary was a carrier of the pneumonia-causing bacteria. 3. The common cold, caused by Rhino viruses, affects the lungs. 4. Pneumonia symptoms include fever, chills, and respiratory difficulties.

133742.subject: Zoology
133742.text: Can sewage be discharged directly into natural water bodies like rivers and streams?
133742.sol: Large quantities of waste water are generated everyday in cities and towns. A major component of this waste water is human excreta. This municipal waste-water is also called sewage. It contains large amounts of organic matter and microbes. Many of which are pathogenic .This huge amount of sewage cannot be discharged into natural water bodies like rivers and streams directly.

133862.subject: Zoology
133862.text: Physical removal of large and small particle from the sewage through filtration and sedimentation is called
133862.sol: Primary treatment : These treatment steps basically involve physical removal of particles – large and small – from the sewage through filtration and sedimentation. These are removed in stages; initially, floating debris is removed by sequential filtration. Then the grit (soil and small pebbles) are removed by sedimentation. All solids that settle form the primary sludge, and the supernatant forms the effluent. The effluent from the primary settling tank is taken for secondary treatment.

133911.subject: Zoology
133911.text: Microbe Application A. Acetobacter 1. Biofertilizer B. Anabaena 2. Antibiotic C. Bacillus 3. Vinegar production D. Penicillin 4. Biopesticide
133911.sol: Acetobacter is used in vinegar production. Anabaena acts as a biofertilizer. Bacillus is used as a biopesticide. Penicillin is an antibiotic.

133985.subject: Zoology
133985.sol: Cyclosporin is used as immunosuppressant. This drug is derived from a fungus, Trichoderma polysporum and is used to prevent rejection of kidney, heart and liver transplants. Cyclosporin inhibits the activity of helper T-cells that act against foreign bodies.

134200.subject: Zoology
134200.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: One can remove the meristem and grow it in vitro to obtain virus-free plants. Reason: Even if the plant is infected with a virus, the meristem is free of virus.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
134200.sol: Even if the plant is infected with a virus, the meristem is free of virus. Hence, one can remove the meristem and grow it in vitro to obtain virus-free plants.

134701.sol: Proteases are the enzymes which digest the protein present inside the cell. Proteases ensure the isolation of DNA without its contamination with proteins.

6a252ff198efbb6c17e929c1.text: Carbonyl compounds undergo a variety of nucleophilic reactions. Which of the following derivatives of cyclohexanone is formed strictly via a nucleophilic addition mechanism, without any subsequent elimination of a small molecule like water?
6a252ff198efbb6c17e929c1.sol: The formation of cyclohexanone cyanohydrin involves the reaction of cyclohexanone with hydrogen cyanide (HCN). The cyanide ion ( CN^- ) acts as a nucleophile and attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon, forming a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate. This intermediate is then protonated to yield the cyanohydrin. The entire process is a pure nucleophilic addition reaction, and no small molecule like water is eliminated. In contrast, the formation of cyclohexanone oxime (from hydroxylamine), cyclohexanone semicarbazon

6a2a77bcfad2360f42564b8f.subject: Physics
6a2a77bcfad2360f42564b8f.text: An electric kettle is rated at 1.2 kW for a 240 V supply. If the line voltage drops to 180 V due to heavy load, what will be the actual power consumed by the kettle? (Assume the resistance of the heating element remains constant)
6a2a77bcfad2360f42564b8f.sol: The resistance of the heating element is given by R = V₁^2 P₁ . Since the resistance remains constant, the new power consumed is P₂ = V₂^2 R . Taking the ratio of the powers, we get P₂ = P₁ ( V₂ V₁ )^2 . Substituting the given values P₁ = 1200 W, V₁ = 240 V, and V₂ = 180 V: P₂ = 1200 ( 180 240 )^2 P₂ = 1200 ( 3 4 )^2 P₂ = 1200 9 16 = 675 W. Answer: 675 W

97847.subject: Botany
97847.text: Read the following statements and identify which one is incorrect.
options: Reproduction is not the defining feature of living organisms.
An isolated metabolic reaction outside the body of an organism is non-living.
Human being is the only organism which has self-consciousness.
97847.sol: Mountains can grow with the accumulation of substances on the surface and thus can grow extrinsically. Mules and worker honey bees are living but they cannot reproduce; hence, reproduction is not a defining feature of living organisms. All living organisms are aware or conscious of their surroundings. Only humans are self-aware. Isolated metabolic reactions are non-living things but are surely living reactions. Thus, an isolated metabolic reaction outside the body of an organism is neither living nor non-living.
